question: Should pre-deadline warnings be a config-only lifecycle guarantee across native and ACP sub-agents, sharing an internal intervention primitive—but not thresholds—with inactivity recovery?
rationale: The requested behavior is new policy and configuration surface, and maintainers must choose its cross-runtime guarantee and relationship to the overlapping stall-recovery design before implementation.

options.title: Unified primitive, distinct policies
options.body: Build one internal intervention scheduler, add a config-only absolute-deadline warning, and let inactivity recovery use separate thresholds on the same control path.

options.title: Deadline-only implementation
options.body: Add a narrow warning tied only to `runTimeoutSeconds`, accepting runtime-specific limitations and deferring inactivity recovery integration.

options.title: Keep hard timeout unchanged
options.body: Retain post-timeout partial-progress recovery and require agents or prompts to checkpoint periodically without adding another lifecycle setting.

recommendation.title: Unified primitive, distinct policies
recommendation.body: Build one internal intervention scheduler, add a config-only absolute-deadline warning, and let inactivity recovery use separate thresholds on the same control path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work and review history cover the native, ACP, timeout, and announcement surfaces needed to choose the contract.
